title: HiTOP Factorization Hierarchy
description: Declares one versioned HiTOP factorization as a recursive tree of stable HiTOP base concepts. Every node names the hitop_base_code it plays and a free-text level name (for example Superspectrum, Spectrum, Subfactor, Component, or a factorization-specific refinement) describing the role it occupies in this factorization; nesting under `children` is the factorization's concrete parent-child structure and is what actually orders the tree (hitop:hasTier) -- `level` is descriptive only. A `kind: collection` node represents a factorization-local synthesis of several existing concepts (see docs/factorizations.md section 4) rather than a core Tier concept, so its `code` does not need to exist in ontology/hitop.ttl. A factorization file never redefines a concept's `rdf:type` or `rdfs:subClassOf`; it copies only the concept's `rdfs:label` (and `rdfs:comment`, when present) from the core ontology onto the generated node, purely so the generated file is readable on its own -- the core ontology remains the sole source of truth for these values. Every other node's `code` must already exist in ontology/hitop.ttl. See docs/factorizations.md for the governance model and for how `level` and `kind` map onto the core ontology's hitop:hasLevel/hitop:hasTier vocabulary.

hierarchy.description: Root node of the factorization tree. May be null only while meta.status is "draft" and the tree has not been populated yet.

factorization_id.description: Stable kebab-case identifier matching the factorizations/<factorization_id> directory name.

version.description: Version identifier matching the leading <version>_hierarchy.yaml filename segment and the v<N> directory, for example "V1052k" in v1/V1052k_hierarchy.yaml.

source.description: Origin of the factor structure, for example a source image or dataset path.

paper.description: Citation for the publication this factorization is derived from.

ontology_iri.description: IRI of the core ontology this factorization resolves codes against.

ontology_version.description: owl:versionInfo value of the ontology release the codes were resolved against.

commit.description: Optional git commit hash pinning the exact ontology state the codes were resolved against.

created_by.description: Person or role who curated this factorization.

created_at.description: Date this factorization version was created.

notes.description: Optional free-text provenance notes, for example differences from a previous version.

level.description: Free-text hitop:hasLevel value naming the role this node plays in this factorization (for example Superspectrum, Spectrum, Subfactor, Component, or a factorization-specific refinement such as Sub-subfactor). Not restricted to a fixed vocabulary and not checked for depth consistency: real HiTOP branches legitimately skip levels (e.g. a Spectrum going straight to Component without an intervening Subfactor), so the same label can occur at different depths across a tree. Vertical ordering itself comes entirely from `children` nesting (hitop:hasTier), not from this value.

kind.description: Whether this node references an existing core Tier concept ("concept", the default) or is a factorization-local synthesis of several existing concepts ("collection", modeled as a skos:Collection; see docs/factorizations.md section 4). Only "collection" nodes are exempt from the requirement that `code` exists in ontology/hitop.ttl.

label.description: Human-readable name of the HiTOP concept (or, for a collection node, the synthesis) at this node.

code.description: For kind "concept": the hitop_base_code from ontology/hitop.ttl that this node names. For kind "collection": a stable, factorization-local identifier that is not looked up in the core ontology.

bridge.description: Documentation-only cross-loading note: other node labels this concept is also empirically associated with in the source paper. Does not create a second hitop:hasTier edge and is not validated against codes.

provisional.description: Marks this node's placement as tentative, independent of the file-level meta.status.

children.description: Child nodes one level step below this node, per hitop:hasTier. For a collection node, its children are exactly the existing concepts being synthesized.
